The region enclosed by the curves $x+{y}^{2}=25$ and $x+5y=25$ for $y\in [0,5]$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $x=25.$ Find the volume $V$ of the resulting solid. Do not round the answer.

$V=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, since we are rotating about a vertical line, we need to solve the equations of our curves for $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}x+{y}^{2} & =25\,⟹\,x=25-{y}^{2} \\ x+5y & =25\,⟹\,x=25-5y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/f5b7cafc0ad6ab7624c1274451f16ba2c3c9a111ac9dad3abd90f082cc42d9b9.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $x=25-{y}^{2},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $x=25-5y.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x=25-5y.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/166dbb3f75000dfc155abfc3452ff6874dab1542409edc7e4867c5a5ee73c0b0.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{5}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{5}{[\,(25)-(25-5y)\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{5}{[5y]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x=25-{y}^{2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/9322b6f4bc9a0e913670f8dcbc9657206c3ae6a30de2f26308054d75b67d0861.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{5}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{5}[\,(25)-(25-{y}^{2})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{5}[{y}^{2}]^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{5}({(5y)}^{2}-{({y}^{2})}^{2})\,\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{5}(25{y}^{2}-{y}^{4})\,\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {(\frac{25{y}^{3}}{3}-\frac{{y}^{5}}{5})|}_{0}^{5} \\  & =\pi [(\frac{25(5)^{3}}{3}-\frac{(5)^{5}}{5})-0] \\  & =\pi (\frac{3125}{3}-625) \\  & =\frac{1250\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
